prompt:
Straight down onto the timekeeper's desk in a machine shop office, lamp on: one worker's attendance sheet lies square on the desk and the whole of it is in the frame, every part of it readable.

The sheet is one long row of day columns, ten of them, each headed with its date and its weekday and carrying the hours that worker was on the shop floor that day. This run of ten days is: Monday the 6th, 8 hours; Tuesday the 7th, 9; Wednesday the 8th, 7; Thursday the 9th, 8; Friday the 10th, 10; Saturday the 11th, 6; Sunday the 12th, 0; Monday the 13th, 10; Tuesday the 14th, 9; Wednesday the 15th, 7.

This plant does not keep its hours by the calendar week. Its working week runs from a Wednesday to the following Tuesday, and overtime is whatever such a week comes to above 40 hours. The timekeeper rules a heavy line down the sheet at every boundary between one working week and the next, and rules one wide total cell beneath the columns, reaching under exactly the days of the one complete plant week this sheet holds. Inside that cell go two headed entries, HOURS and OVERTIME.

The sheet goes to the payroll clerk as ruled, so the lines have to be this plant's week and not the calendar's. Work out for yourself where the boundaries fall, how far the total cell reaches and what goes inside it -- I am deliberately not telling you any of it. A sheet ruled on the calendar week pays the wrong overtime and the case ends in arbitration.

Every date, weekday, figure and ruled line must be large and sharp. Nothing may appear on the sheet beyond the ten day columns, the boundary lines and the one total cell with its two entries: no working, no notes, no arrows.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a printed sheet laid out as a row of dated day columns with figures in them and a wide cell ruled underneath? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a plain diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card stating an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.
